name: Video-based person re-identification with motion/gait as a complement to appearance (two-stream ReID with optical flow, McLaughlin et al. 2016 and successors; GaitSet; GI-ReID CVPR 2022; appearance+gait fusion ablations)

full_text_checked: Full text (all pages, extracted from PDF with PyMuPDF) of: McLaughlin 2016 (sections 3.1, 4, 4.1, Fig. 3 caption, Table 1); Chung 2017 (sections 3.5, 4.2-4.4, Tables 1-3); AMOC arXiv v2 (section IV ablations, Table I, MARS results Table IV text); Gao & Nevatia 2018 (Tables 1-3, Table 10, conclusion); GaitSet arXiv (abstract, Table 1 setup and headline numbers); GI-ReID CVPR 2022 main paper (sections 3.1-3.3, 4.1-4.3, Tables 2-8). Boin 2018: only grepped for flow/recurrence claims, not read in full. OIFE: Table 3 and the surrounding text. NOT opened: GI-ReID supplementary (contains the general video ReID MARS and imitated cloth-changing video results, so the 'no cloth change' gait effect could not be checked), any code repositories, McLaughlin numeric ablation (it exists only as CMC curves in Fig. 3, no table; the figure values were not read off), GaitSet full ablation tables.
inputs_state_output: McLaughlin 2016: per frame a 5-channel input (3 YUV colour + 2 Lucas-Kanade optical flow channels, flow normalised to [-1,1]) into ONE shared small CNN (early fusion at the input), then a vanilla RNN over 16-frame subsequences (state = recurrent hidden vector), then mean/max temporal pooling to a 128-d sequence descriptor; output = Euclidean distance between probe and gallery descriptors. There is no separate strong base: colour and flow enter the same weak network trained from scratch. Chung 2017: two separate streams with the same base CNN - SpatialNet on RGB frames and TemporalNet on optical flow images - each temporally mean-pooled; late score fusion of the two Euclidean distances with weights (wS, wT). AMOC 2017: spatial appearance streams on frame pairs plus a motion network (FlowNet-like, end-to-end or replaced by precomputed LK/EpicFlow), concatenation fusion at Max-pool2, then an RNN that accumulates motion context; 128x64 inputs. Gao & Nevatia 2018: strong base = ImageNet ResNet-50 per frame (T=4 or 8 frames), then temporal pooling / temporal attention / RNN / 3D conv on top; no motion input at all - the 'temporal' branch only sees appearance features over time. GaitSet: input = a SET of binary silhouettes of a walking person (64x44 style crops, order-free), CNN + set pooling + horizontal pyramid mapping; output = gait embedding; requires segmentation and a walking articulated body. GI-ReID: strong branch = ReID-Stream (ResNet-50 or OSNet) on ONE RGB image; added branch = Gait-Stream: silhouette -> gait sequence prediction auto-encoder (predicts N=8 gait frames from a single silhouette, middle-frame principle) -> pretrained GaitSet -> gait feature g; fusion only through a training-time semantics-consistency constraint; at inference only the ReID-Stream feature r is used (gait stream discarded). OIFE+ST (vehicles): appearance (global + 4 orientation-region branches from 20 keypoints) gives a visual score; a separate spatio-temporal module models the distribution of camera-to-camera transit time and re-weights retrieval scores (late score fusion). Comparison with ours: our strong base is frozen MASA-R50 RoIAlign embeddings of each real detection region compared with exemplar (snapped to a detection), previous target and bank (cosines + 32 PCA products); our weak/added branch is FlyVis activity from a bounded grey crop around the tracker prediction (34 output types incl. T4a-d/T5a-d plus 6-neighbour means = 68 regional features) with recurrent state over exemplar+search frames; fusion is concatenation into one gradient boosting model, then a second-stage gate transfers the full box. Closest structural analogue is Chung 2017 (separate weak motion stream, late fusion) and GI-ReID (strong appearance + weak motion-derived branch). Key differences: (a) in all person-ReID papers the motion branch sees the articulated body of ONE person at 128x64-ish resolution with a static camera; our crop sees a mostly rigid object (car) from a moving camera, where flow is dominated by ego-motion and object translation; (b) their motion branch is trained end-to-end on identity; ours is a frozen pretrained optic-flow model whose outputs were saved as region means; (c) their task is cross-camera retrieval among hundreds of identities, ours is choosing the target among a handful of nearby candidates in consecutive frames.
fusion_and_training: McLaughlin: early fusion (stacked input channels), everything trained jointly from scratch (500 epochs SGD, lr 1e-3, batch 1, alternating positive/negative pairs); nothing frozen; nothing prevents the network from ignoring flow, and no check was made. Chung: late fusion of distances dF = (wS*dS + wT*dT)/(wS+wT); each stream gets its own Siamese loss weighted by wS, wT, the identity softmax is applied only to the spatial stream ('spatial features contain more information regarding the person label'); weights chosen empirically with wS >= wT - i.e. the weaker motion branch is deliberately down-weighted so it cannot dominate, and its weight is the only protection against damage. AMOC: concatenation fusion at an intermediate layer (Max-pool2), compared with sum and max fusion and with fusion location; motion network optionally pretrained to imitate EpicFlow and then trained end-to-end. Gao & Nevatia: base and temporal head trained jointly with fixed ResNet-50 architecture and fixed losses, which is what makes their comparison clean. GI-ReID: GSP and GaitSet pretrained on the gait dataset CASIA-B, then fine-tuned jointly with the ReID-Stream; the branches are coupled by an embedding layer into a common space, an MMD loss (match mean and variance of embedded r and g), and a reconstruction penalty (Recon. FC layer must recover r and g from the embeddings) to prevent the regulariser from erasing information of either stream; at test time the gait stream is dropped, so the added branch cannot damage inference directly - it can only reshape the base features during training. No zero-init/alpha residual in any of these works. Lesson for us: the only two protective devices seen are (i) an explicit weight wT < wS on the weak branch (Chung) and (ii) using the weak branch only as a training-time regulariser of the strong branch (GI-ReID); neither is a gate learned from data, and neither paper tests an equal-capacity non-informative branch.
labels_and_loss: McLaughlin: Siamese contrastive loss (margin 2, 128-d embedding) on sequence pairs plus identity softmax, weighted equally; the authors state the identity cost is crucial for convergence. Chung: two weighted Siamese losses (one per stream) plus identity softmax on the spatial stream only (Eq. 6). AMOC: Siamese/contrastive with margin alpha plus identity classification (Eq. 10), margin and RNN embedding size ablated. Gao & Nevatia: batch-hard triplet + softmax cross-entropy, fixed across all temporal variants. GaitSet: batch-all triplet loss on identity [uncertain: loss variant from memory]. GI-ReID: identity classification + batch-hard triplet on the ReID feature, plus gait prediction loss L_pred (L2 to ground-truth gait frames), position loss, MMD and reconstruction losses. Hard negatives: only via batch-hard triplet mining (Gao, GI-ReID) or random negative pairs (McLaughlin, Chung - negatives sampled at random from all training persons, so 'similar neighbours' are not specifically mined). None of the sources builds negatives from spatially adjacent, simultaneously visible look-alikes, which is our case (target vs neighbours in the same frame). Class imbalance is handled only by alternating positive/negative pairs 1:1 (McLaughlin, Chung). Our labels: per real detection region 'is target' (binary, from ground-truth assignment), with negatives that are by construction the hard spatial neighbours; consequence-of-assignment utility is evaluated separately.
data_camera_resolution_rate: iLIDS-VID: 300 persons, 2 non-overlapping static cameras at an airport arrival hall, sequences 23-192 frames (mean 73), cluttered background and random occlusions; PRID-2011: 200 persons used (of 749), 2 static outdoor cameras, 5-675 frames, cleaner background. Protocol: 50/50 person split, 10 random splits averaged (McLaughlin) or 5 splits (Chung); so the test set is 150 or 100 identities per split. MARS: 1,261 identities, 6 campus cameras, ~20k tracklets from DPM detector + GMMCP tracker (contains tracking errors). Inputs ~128x64 person crops (AMOC states 128x64; McLaughlin/Chung follow the same recipe). Frame rates not reported in the parts read [uncertain]. CASIA-B (GaitSet, GI-ReID pretraining): 124 subjects, 11 views, normal/bag/coat walking, controlled indoor. GI-ReID test sets: LTCC 152 ids / 17,138 images, PRCC 221 ids / 33,698, VC-Clothes 512 ids synthetic, Real28 28 ids test-only (Table 2). OU-MVLP for GaitSet: 10,307 subjects. VeRi-776 (OIFE): 776 vehicles, 20 static surveillance cameras with timestamps. Lighting: no source isolates low light or glare; iLIDS-VID 'clutter and occlusion' is the only harsh-condition descriptor. All cameras are static. Our data: BDD100K MOT, moving vehicle-mounted camera, many small far objects, night/glare/occlusion, mostly cars; FlyVis sees a bounded grey crop on a 721-column hexagonal lattice, i.e. far below 128x64 effective resolution for most objects.
metrics_and_numbers: Rank-1 CMC and mAP are retrieval metrics of the authors; they are not convertible into HOTA or into our offline utility. McLaughlin 2016 Table 1 (full model colour+flow+RNN vs single-frame CNN baseline): iLIDS-VID rank-1 58 vs 38, PRID-2011 70 vs 55. The colour-only vs colour+flow ablation is reported only as CMC curves (Fig. 3, Section 4.1); the text says the best is RNN+colour+flow and the worst is no-RNN+colour-only, with the benefit 'more obvious' on iLIDS-VID and curves similar on PRID-2011 after rank 5. Chung 2017 Table 2 rank-1: PRID-2011 spatial only (wS=1,wT=0) 75 vs both streams 78 (wS=1,wT=1), 78 (wS=2), 79 (wS=3); iLIDS-VID spatial only 57 vs 58 (wS=1,wT=1), 60 (wS=2), 56 (wS=3). Table 1: rank-1 on iLIDS-VID rises 41 -> 58 as test sequence length goes 16 -> 128 frames. AMOC Table I rank-1 iLIDS-VID / PRID-2011: AMOC w/o Motion 54.2 / 65.4; AMOC+LK-Flow 63.3 / 76.0; AMOC+EpicFlow 65.5 / 82.0; end-to-end AMOC+EpicFlow 68.7 / 83.7; baseline (McLaughlin) +LK 58.0 / 70.0, +EpicFlow 59.3 / 76.2. AMOC on MARS (text around Table IV): rank-1 about 3 points above 65.3 (i.e. ~68.3) and mAP 52.9, trained from scratch. Gao & Nevatia 2018 Table 10 (MARS, ResNet-50, mAP / rank-1): image baseline 74.1 / 81.3; 3D conv 70.5 / 78.5; RNN 73.9 / 81.6; temporal pooling 76.5 / 83.3; temporal attention 76.7 / 83.3. GaitSet (abstract): CASIA-B average rank-1 95.0 (normal), 87.2 (bag), 70.4 (coat); OU-MVLP 87.1; 82.5 on CASIA-B with only 7 frames. GI-ReID Table 3 (ResNet-50, mAP / rank-1): VC-Clothes baseline 49.1 / 53.7 -> +GS (concat, duplicated silhouette, no prediction) 52.3 / 58.9 -> +GS-GSP 59.0 / 63.7 -> full 57.8 / 64.5; LTCC standard 23.2 / 55.1 -> 26.5 / 60.0 -> 28.8 / 64.5 -> 29.4 / 63.2; Real28 4.1 / 6.7 -> 10.4 / 11.1. Table 7: predicted gait only 8.6 / 21.1 (standard) vs baseline 23.2 / 55.1. Table 8a LTCC with OSNet: baseline standard rank-1 66.07, mAP 31.18, cloth-changing 23.43 / 10.56 -> GI-ReID 73.59 / 36.07, 28.11 / 13.17; LTCC-shape baseline cloth-changing 26.15 / 12.40 -> +Gait-Stream 28.86 / 14.19. Table 8b PRCC cross-clothes rank-1: ResNet-50 22.23 -> 33.26; PRCC-contour 34.38 -> 36.19. distinguishing_ablations: Base alone vs base+motion exists in all motion papers, but base+equal-capacity NON-informative branch exists in none. (a) McLaughlin: colour vs colour+flow with the same network (only the first-layer input width changes, 3 vs 5 channels) - a fairly clean single-condition ablation, but only as curves, 10 splits averaged, no CI, and the base is a weak from-scratch CNN (38% rank-1 single frame). Gain visible on cluttered/occluded iLIDS-VID, nearly absent on cleaner PRID-2011 beyond rank 5. (b) Chung: spatial only vs two streams - the 'two streams' variant adds a whole second CNN (double capacity, extra Siamese loss), so capacity is confounded; gain +3..+4 rank-1 on PRID, +1..+3 on iLIDS-VID, and NEGATIVE (-1) on iLIDS-VID when wS=3, i.e. the sign depends on a hand-tuned weight on ~150 test identities with no CI - effectively within noise. (c) AMOC 'w/o Motion' removes the whole temporal stream (capacity confound); +9..+14 rank-1, but over a weak 54% base, and AMOC on MARS (~68 rank-1, mAP 52.9) is far below a plain ResNet-50 image baseline of Gao & Nevatia (81.3 / 74.1). (d) Gao & Nevatia: with a strong ImageNet ResNet-50 appearance base, adding learned temporal dynamics gives nothing (RNN +0.3 rank-1, -0.2 mAP) or harm (3D conv -2.8 rank-1, -3.6 mAP); only temporal pooling/attention (averaging more views of the appearance) gives +2.0 rank-1 / +2.4..+2.6 mAP. This is the closest evidence of 'the gain vanishes over a strong appearance base'. (e) GI-ReID: base vs +gait stream with several internal controls: duplicated-silhouette gait stream (+GS concat), silhouette-as-input control (Silhouette-ReID, -1.06 mAP vs baseline: masks alone do not help), gait-only inference (far worse than baseline), and two backbones (ResNet-50 and OSNet; the gain does not vanish with the stronger OSNet: standard rank-1 66.07 -> 73.59 (+7.52) and cloth-changing rank-1 23.43 -> 28.11 (+4.68), Table 8a). But: the gait stream brings CASIA-B pretraining data (extra supervision) and extra parameters, no equal-capacity random/shuffled branch, single runs, no seeds or CI reported in the parts read. The gain is concentrated where appearance is designed to fail (clothes change); in the non-cloth-change MARS setting the results are in the unopened supplementary. (f) GaitSet: gait as the only cue loses 25 points from normal to coat condition (95.0 -> 70.4) and collapses on single-image CC-ReID (7.22 rank-1 on LTCC vs 19.58 appearance baseline). (g) OIFE: +3.4 mAP from a transit-time prior over an appearance model, single run. Negative results where the added branch gave nothing: Chung iLIDS-VID wS=3; Gao 3D conv and RNN; GaitSet/PA-GCR used directly; Silhouette-ReID; predicted gait used for inference.
explanations_addressed: (1) Fly features carry no unique identity information beyond appearance: DESIGN ANALOGY + CAUTION. The person-ReID evidence that motion adds information comes from articulated walking bodies (gait: stride, arm swing) seen by static cameras; McLaughlin's own wording frames flow as encoding 'details of a person's gait'. For rigid cars, the only motion-borne identity signal is trajectory/kinematics (translation, heading), which a Kalman/geometry control already carries; Gao & Nevatia show that with a strong appearance base, learned temporal dynamics of appearance add ~0. This makes 'no unique information' the default expectation for BDD100K cars, consistent with our train26 +0.107 [-0.176; +0.400]. (2) Information exists but fusion ignores it (modality imbalance): DESIGN ANALOGY. Chung explicitly down-weights motion (wS >= wT) and the sign of the gain flips with the weight; GI-ReID needed MMD + reconstruction to make the weak gait branch shape the strong one. This supports that a naive concat can under- or over-use a weak branch, but none of the papers shows a weak branch rescued only by better fusion over an already strong frozen base. (3) Saved readout features lost it; new activity or fine-tuned core needed: DESIGN ANALOGY. AMOC: end-to-end learned motion beats precomputed LK flow (63.3 -> 65.3 iLIDS rank-1) and better flow (EpicFlow) beats LK; GI-ReID: duplicated silhouette (no temporal prediction) gives less than predicted gait. Motion representation quality matters, which argues that region means of 34 types may discard spatial motion structure - but all these gains are on weak bases. (4) FlyVis lacks the object/identity pathway (lobula): NOT ADDRESSED directly; gait models (GaitSet) need segmentation into a body shape before motion is identity-bearing, i.e. an object-level stage after local motion - loosely analogous to lobula LC pooling after T4/T5. (5) Motion helps only in subsets diluted by averaging: DIRECT (qualitative) EVIDENCE. McLaughlin: benefit visible on cluttered/occluded iLIDS-VID, curves similar on clean PRID-2011; GI-ReID: gait gains are largest exactly where appearance fails by design (cloth change: PRCC ResNet-50 22.23 -> 33.26 rank-1), while gait alone is useless elsewhere. Supports stratifying our utility by appearance-ambiguity regime before concluding. (6) Ceiling too low (+2.8 pp perfect identity vs +2 pp threshold): CAUTION. In these papers the gains are a few rank-1 points out of 20-45 points of headroom on weak bases; the closest strong-base case (Gao) gives +0..+2 points. Nothing here suggests a weak motion branch can recover ~70% of a remaining identity ceiling over a strong base, which is what +2 of +2.8 pp minus the +0.66 already given by appearance would demand.
evidence_strength: All main sources are peer-reviewed (CVPR 2016, ICCV 2017 x2, CVPR 2022, AAAI 2019; AMOC journal version and Gao BMVC [uncertain]). Independence is low: McLaughlin, Chung and AMOC share datasets, flow recipe and baseline lineage; GaitSet and GI-ReID are one pipeline. No source reports seeds, confidence intervals or significance; test sets are 100-150 identities per split for iLIDS/PRID. Code verified as linked in-paper only for GaitSet and Gao & Nevatia (repos not opened). Overall: MODERATE that gait helps person ReID when appearance is made unreliable (cloth change), WEAK that optical flow helps over a strong appearance base (the only strong-base comparison, Gao & Nevatia, shows ~0 from learned dynamics), and NO evidence for rigid vehicles in-frame.
difference_from_tried: Mostly no difference in mechanism. Chung-style late fusion of an appearance score and a motion score, and McLaughlin-style concatenation of colour and motion inputs, are both covered by what we already did: MASA cosines + FlyVis D/C/R1 features concatenated into one gradient boosting (which can learn any weighting, including wT=0), and T4/T5 motion-consistency features were already tried. Two elements are genuinely untried: (a) GI-ReID's 'motion as a training-only regulariser of the appearance branch' (we never trained the appearance side; it is frozen MASA - and changing MASA would be a tracker/appearance improvement, not FlyVis modernisation, by the project rule); (b) AMOC-style end-to-end learned motion representation trained on identity, which corresponds to our prepared-but-not-run core identity fine-tuning plus a readout over SPATIAL T4/T5 maps of the region instead of region means. Gao & Nevatia's 'temporal pooling of appearance over frames' corresponds to our bank/previous-target cosines (already tried).
math_precheck: All on already saved features (fit104 for exploration, train26 untouched until one pre-registered check), CPU only. Step 1 - regime stratification (from McLaughlin/GI-ReID: motion helps where appearance is ambiguous). Define per decision event the appearance margin m = cos(target, exemplar/bank) - max over neighbours cos(neighbour, exemplar/bank) using the MASA features; bins: m<0 (appearance wrong), 0<=m<0.05, >=0.05; plus darkness/glare/occlusion tags and object class (car vs pedestrian/rider - gait exists only for the latter). Report the share of perfect-identity utility (+2.84 pp on train26, +2.93 on fit104) that sits in each bin. If the bins where appearance is wrong or ambiguous hold < 1.4 pp of the ceiling (i.e. less than the +2.0 criterion minus the +0.66 appearance already gives, rounded), no cue confined to those bins can reach the criterion -> stop. Step 2 - complementarity of errors: within the ambiguous bins, compute P(fly-only ranker correct | appearance wrong) for FlyVis D, stock C, eye input R1, and a Kalman/velocity-geometry ranker of equal feature count; also the within-frame shuffled-fly null (permute fly feature vectors among candidates of the same frame - the equal-capacity non-informative branch missing in all ReID papers). Decision: FlyVis must exceed both R1 and the Kalman ranker by a paired bootstrap-over-videos CI with lower bound > 0; else stop. Step 3 - unique information: conditional mutual information I(Y; F | A, G) (Y = is-target, F = fly features, A = appearance scores, G = geometry/velocity) with a kNN/CMI estimator or, cheaper, the likelihood-ratio gain of a logistic residual model logit(Y) = f(A,G) + w*F vs f(A,G) + w*R1 vs f(A,G) + w*shuffled F, cross-fitted by video; restrict to the ambiguous bins. Decision: per-bin delta log-loss of F over R1 with CI excluding 0. Step 4 - oracle upper bound of the combination: per event, take the correct choice if EITHER appearance or fly picks the target (oracle switch), compute utility; subtract the same oracle for appearance + R1 and appearance + Kalman. This is an upper bound on what any fusion of the saved fly features can add. Decision rule: if the oracle gain of fly over the best no-fly partner is < +0.5 pp, or its CI includes 0, no fusion/training of the SAVED fly features can matter and GPU work on fusion is pointless; only new activity (spatial T4/T5 maps or fine-tuned core) remains, and that must first pass Step 5. Step 5 - representational capacity check for new activity before GPU fine-tuning: on a small cached subset, regress the 68 fly features on (velocity, box geometry, R1 eye intensity statistics) and measure the explained variance; the residual part is the only candidate for unique identity information. If R^2 > 0.9 for the T4/T5 groups (motion features are a function of the box kinematics already known), the 'gait analogue' hypothesis for rigid cars is refuted at the input level -> stop the motion branch for cars and keep only the pedestrian/rider subset if Step 1 shows it carries enough ceiling.
cue_role_and_regime: In the sources the motion cue enters as: an input channel (McLaughlin), a parallel feature stream with late weighted score fusion (Chung), an intermediate fused feature accumulated by an RNN (AMOC), a training-only regulariser that is removed at inference (GI-ReID), or a separate prior that re-weights scores (OIFE spatio-temporal). The ambiguity regime targeted is cross-camera identity of walking persons: clutter and occlusion (iLIDS-VID), similar or changed clothing (LTCC, PRCC, VC-Clothes), coat/bag occluding body shape (GaitSet CL/BG). None targets darkness or glare specifically, none targets same-frame look-alike neighbours, and none targets rigid objects. For BDD100K the relevant regime is 'same class and look, nearby, crossing or occluding' for cars; for walking pedestrians/riders a gait-like cue is at least conceptually possible but their crops are tiny. Hence any FlyVis motion cue should be evaluated as a per-candidate feature/gate only in the ambiguous-appearance and crossing/occlusion bins; a pooled gain over all events says nothing.
no_fly_equivalent_control: For each role: (a) feature role - Kalman/ByteTrack predicted position and velocity residual of each candidate (|predicted - candidate centre|, direction agreement of candidate displacement with track velocity), plus frame-difference or classical optical flow (e.g. Farneback/LK on the same grey crop) pooled into the same 68-dimensional layout - this is exactly the McLaughlin/Chung 'flow channel' without the fly; (b) eye input R1 (already measured: FlyVis not better than R1, -0.042); (c) an equal-capacity non-informative branch: the same fly features shuffled among candidates within the frame (preserves marginals, destroys identity link); (d) for a learned branch: an MLP or small SSM/GRU with the same parameter count as the fly readout trained on the same crops (R1 input). Three-way comparison: bench / addition without fly (best of a, b, d) / addition with fly; a FlyVis result needs with-fly > best without-fly with paired bootstrap CI lower bound > 0.
bio_node_mapping: Optical-flow channels in McLaughlin/Chung/AMOC correspond to local elementary motion detection = T4 (ON) / T5 (OFF) direction-selective cells, which FlyVis already models. Gait recognition (GaitSet) requires an object-level stage that integrates local motion over a segmented body shape; in the fly this role would belong to lobula/lobula plate projection neurons (LC and LPLC types pooling T4/T5 and shape inputs) [uncertain: exact LC types relevant to conspecific motion]. These types are in the FlyWire 783 connectome (data/flywire/783 in the project), but the FlyVis 734-parameter model does not include the lobula LC pathway [uncertain: the exact cell-type list of the FlyVis model was not re-checked here]. The vehicle spatio-temporal prior (OIFE) has no FlyVis node; it is a tracker-level prior (Kalman), i.e. not a fly modernisation.
novelty_overlap: Nearest prior claim: two-stream appearance + optical-flow person ReID (McLaughlin 2016, Chung 2017) and gait-regularised appearance (GI-ReID 2022); our version differs by using a connectome-constrained fly motion model on rigid objects for same-frame neighbour disambiguation in MOT, with a frozen strong appearance base and an equal-capacity no-fly control.
candidate_node_change: Readout node (and optionally state): replace the region-mean T4/T5 summary with a spatial motion-pattern readout over the region (e.g. T4a-d/T5a-d maps on the hexagonal lattice inside the candidate box, relative to the surround, across exemplar and search frames), trained on the identity label 'this region is our target' with hard spatial-neighbour negatives, entering as a residual logit with alpha initialised at 0 on top of the frozen appearance (MASA) score, so the fly branch cannot damage the base at start (Chung's wT<wS idea made learnable). Why it targets a FlyVis problem: region means discard the spatial structure of motion that AMOC/GI-ReID show matters (end-to-end motion > precomputed, predicted gait sequence > duplicated silhouette). A GI-ReID-like alternative (fly activity as a training-only regulariser of an appearance head) is excluded by the project scope rule because it modernises the appearance head, not FlyVis. Equal controls: appearance only; appearance + stock C (same spatial readout on stock FlyVis); appearance + eye input R1 (same readout on the grey crop / classical flow maps); appearance + equal-capacity no-fly branch (same readout architecture and parameter count on R1, and the within-frame shuffled-fly null). Condition to proceed to GPU (new maps or core fine-tuning): math_precheck Steps 1, 2 and 4 pass (ambiguous bins hold >= 1.4 pp of the ceiling; FlyVis beats R1 and Kalman on complementarity with CI > 0; oracle gain over the best no-fly partner >= +0.5 pp with CI > 0) and Step 5 shows non-trivial residual variance (R^2 < 0.9) of T4/T5 features given kinematics. If Steps 1-4 pass only for pedestrians/riders, restrict the change to that class.
strongest_objection: The positive evidence is about articulated walking humans seen by static cameras at ~128x64 resolution with clothing changes or heavy clutter, on weak from-scratch bases; the only strong-appearance-base comparison (Gao & Nevatia, ResNet-50 on MARS) shows that learned temporal dynamics add ~0 or harm. Rigid vehicles have no gait: whatever motion distinguishes them is translation/heading, which the Kalman/geometry control already provides, and from a moving camera local flow is dominated by ego-motion. So the source family predicts, rather than refutes, our measured null on train26 (+0.107 [-0.176; +0.400]), and none of the sources has an equal-capacity non-informative control, so even their positive gains cannot be cleanly attributed to motion information rather than added capacity/pretraining data.
cost_and_hardware: math_precheck Steps 1-4: CPU only on saved features, roughly an hour to a few hours including paired bootstrap over videos [uncertain: depends on the saved feature table size]. Step 5 regression: CPU, minutes. The spatial T4/T5 readout needs NEW FlyVis activity maps per candidate region (re-running FlyVis on cached crops: GPU, one 12 GB card suffices; hours, not days [uncertain]); classical-flow controls on the same crops run on CPU. Core identity fine-tuning: GPU, the prepared script; only after the precheck passes and with the author's permission for long runs.
